chapter: Nonet, later partnerships and recent projects
title: The 1974 session with Chet Baker and Keith Jarrett
summary: They discuss a TV quartet and a record at Ornette's studio.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Let’s move on into the seventies. Here are a couple of interesting records: Lee Konitz with Chet Baker and Keith Jarrett from WNYC TV “Jazz Adventures” broadcast.
Keith actually asked to be apart of that. It was just a quartet with Charlie Haden and . . .
It was the first time I heard Keith playing standards and I was very impressed.
Now of course he does it a lot.
Yeah. Made a career out of it.
Yeah. Then there’s a record for Indian Navigation. A quartet record with you, Chet, Michael Moore, and Beaver Harris.
Yeah at Ornette’s studio. I remember Ornette standing there with a video camera filming some of that and Chet not being in too good condition for whatever reason.
He was just getting back on the scene then in seventy-four after being off for several years I guess getting new dentures and whatever and being able to play again.
